evaluator.name: METR
evaluator.summary: Reference evaluator for autonomy and AI R&D capability. Named by Anthropic as the model for embedded evaluators in September 2026; led the on-site investigation of the OpenAI agent swarm incident.
evaluator.funding_tension: Funding is scored 3. The decision applies the case for 3: bounded negatives re-derived from primary filings — no METR-named grant in the Good Ventures, Pew, Packard, Schmidt-family, or TED filings checked, and no direct Coefficient grant in the 2,911-row index — float the value to a floor of 3 under F.13 (metr.24, metr.16), and the current no-lab-money rule bars donations made by or at the direction of frontier AI company employees (metr.18). The contrary funding evidence is retained as dissent: that rule is recent and its wording has moved — absent in April 2024, a compensation footnote in April 2025, and a September 2025 footnote that still accepted donations from individual lab employees, with an OpenAI technical lead among the named individual donors (metr.14); about $21M arrives through donor-advised funds and the Audacious Project with non-public underlying donors, including a $4M Vanguard Charitable grant (metr.15, metr.25); METR's ~$17M Audacious share is not visible in any filing checked (metr.26); second-hop routes run through ARC, Longview, and Constellation, all downstream of Coefficient (metr.21); METR runs on significant free tokens from the labs it evaluates (metr.03); OpenAI set the incident-investigation window and METR incorporated its structure, emphasis, clarity, and tone feedback (metr.06, metr.08); and access remains voluntary while OpenAI kept redaction rights (metr.13, metr.08).
evaluator.what_would_move_the_score: Contract terms for the Anthropic embedded program that fix scope-setting and publication rights in writing, plus a public cooling-off policy.

dissent.lower: Personnel could be 1. A METR director founded FAR.AI, which OpenAI pays for red-teaming; a METR advisor is an a16z partner while a16z backs xAI and Thinking Machines; another advisor advises Thinking Machines; former advisors moved to Anthropic and to the OpenAI Foundation board; a former Anthropic researcher joined in September 2026. If advisors count as leaders, P.2 caps advisory roles at labs at 1, and the August 2026 policy has no cooling-off period.
dissent.higher: Personnel could be 3. The August 2026 conflict-of-interest policy requires staff disclosure before any company-identifying risk assessment, applies provisional recusal, bans direct equity in frontier AI companies, and bars frontier-company employees from the board; advisor and director affiliations are listed on the team page. Anchor 3 asks for a recusal policy and disclosure of lab ties, and both are now published; the one-hop seats are advisory, not lab roles.
